It now means "match the host width", as it already did on `kbq-select`. `fit-content` preserves the old behaviour. Both the static (`panelWidth="auto"`) and bound (`[panelWidth]="'auto'"`) forms are rewritten; a dynamic value (`[panelWidth]="expr"`) is skipped with a warning.

`auto` still type-checks and still renders, the panel is just laid out differently — it isn't the only silent change in this release though, see the `panelWidth={{0}}` note below.

sections.heading: What you need to fix manually
Upgrade to Angular 21
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-version(21.0.0) */}

In version 21.0.0 the library moves to Angular 21. Requirements: **Angular 21+**, **TypeScript 5.9** and **Node.js 20.19, 22.12 or 24+**. Update Angular first, then Koobiq:

```bash
ng update @angular/core@21 @angular/cli@21 @angular/cdk@21
ng update @koobiq/components@21
```

sections.heading: Zoneless change detection
sections.body:
Koobiq components no longer depend on zone.js: they render in an application bootstrapped with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` and keep working with `provideZoneChangeDetection()`. What used to wait for `NgZone.onStable` now runs after the next render.

- **`MockNgZone` is removed** from `@koobiq/components/core`. It fired `onStable` on demand, and nothing in the library listens to it any more: drop the `NgZone` override, and replace `simulateZoneExit()` with `fixture.detectChanges()` or `await fixture.whenStable()`.
- **A spec without zone.js renders only when told to.** A check made right after an event needs `fixture.detectChanges()` or `await fixture.whenStable()` first, and `whenStable()` no longer waits for timers the component started.
- **The actions panel container is `OnPush`**, like the sidepanel container. In an application with zone.js, a component opened in the panel that writes its fields from a timer or a subscription calls `markForCheck()` or keeps that state in a signal.

`zoneless-change-detection` reports every use of `MockNgZone` and `simulateZoneExit()`:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:zoneless-change-detection --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Animations without @angular/animations
sections.body:
Koobiq components no longer use `@angular/animations`, which Angular deprecated: they animate with CSS and wait for the end of an animation themselves. `@angular/animations` is no longer a peer dependency, and the components no longer need `provideAnimations()`: remove it, and the package, unless the components of your application declare `animations: [...]` themselves.

- **The motion is off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.** To turn it off in the whole application, for example in an end-to-end suite, provide `{ provide: KBQ_ANIMATIONS_CONFIG, useValue: { animationsDisabled: true } }` from `@koobiq/components/core`. `provideNoopAnimations()` still turns it off, but it belongs to the deprecated package.
- **The exported triggers are removed**: `fadeAnimation` and `kbqSelectAnimations` from `core`, `kbqDropdownAnimations`, `fadeInItems` and `transformDropdown` from `dropdown`, `kbqTabsAnimations` from `tabs`, `kbqPopoverAnimations` from `popover`, `kbqDatepickerAnimations` from `datepicker`, `KbqNotificationCenterAnimations` from `notification-center` and `kbqAppSwitcherAnimations` from `app-switcher`. `KbqSidepanelAnimationState` is no longer exported from `sidepanel`, nor `MODAL_ANIMATE_DURATION` from `modal`: instead of a timer of that length, act on `afterOpen` / `afterClose` of the `KbqModalRef`.
- **The members that carried an `AnimationEvent` are removed.** `KbqPopUp.animationStart()` and `animationDone()`: a subclass overrides the protected `afterShowAnimation()`, which runs once each time the pop-up appears, not again when the pointer returns to an open one. `KbqDropdown.animationDone`, `isAnimating`, `panelAnimationState`, `startAnimation()`, `resetAnimation()`, `onAnimationStart()` and `onAnimationDone()`: a custom trigger calls `setOpened()`. `KbqSidebar.animationState`, `onAnimationStart()` and `onAnimationDone()`: listen to `stateChanged`. `KbqTabBody.onTranslateTabStarted()` and `onTranslateTabComplete()`, `KbqToastService.animation`, `KbqToastComponent.animationState` and `onAnimation()`, the `animationStateChanged` of the sidepanel and actions panel containers, and `animationState`, `animationTransform` and `setAnimationState()` of the sidepanel container: follow a panel through its ref — `afterOpened()`, `beforeClosed()`, `afterClosed()`. The protected `KbqContentPanelContainer.contentAnimationState` fed the removed `@contentAnimation` trigger: a subclass reads `isOpened()`.
- **The dropdown panel no longer fades out**: it is closed, and its lazy content detached, as soon as the trigger reports it.
- **In a spec, what waited for an animation callback now waits for the next render**: `fixture.detectChanges()` or `await fixture.whenStable()`. jsdom has no Web Animations API, so nothing animates there.

`angular-animations-removal` reports every use of the removed triggers and members:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:angular-animations-removal --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Overlays in the top layer
Color as a signal
sections.body:
`color` of `KbqColorDirective` is a writable signal, and so is the `color` of every component built on it: the buttons, checkbox, toggle, radio, icons, form field, hints, cleaner, progress bar and spinner, and tag. The `[color]` binding is unchanged.

- **A read is a call, a write is `.set()`**: `icon.color()`, `button.color.set(KbqComponentColors.Theme)`. A color set in code holds until the `[color]` binding changes, as an assigned one did.
- **An unset or falsy `[color]` renders the default color of the component**, `kbq-empty` where it has none, instead of no color class.
- **A subclass can no longer override the `color` accessor.** Set its default with `setDefaultColor()` instead of assigning `color` in the constructor. `_color` is removed, `defaultColor` is a signal, and `KbqColorDirective` takes the type of its color as a parameter: `KbqColorDirective` for the buttons. `CanColor` is removed: type the member `Signal`, or use `KbqColorDirective`.

`color-signals` rewrites the reads and writes, and reports subclasses:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:color-signals --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Removed mixins
sections.body:
`mixinDisabled` and `mixinTabIndex` are removed from `@koobiq/components/core` with `CanDisable`, `CanDisableCtor`, `HasTabIndex` and `HasTabIndexCtor`. They were deprecated and unused inside the library: declare `disabled` and `tabIndex` as inputs of the class instead. `core-mixins-removal` reports every use:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:core-mixins-removal --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Options
sections.body:
`KbqOption`, `KbqOptgroup`, the option action and `KbqTimezoneOption` keep their state in signal inputs. The state of an option is still read as a property — `event.option.value`, `select.selected.disabled`, `option.viewValue` in a `kbqSelectTagContent` template — so those reads are unchanged.

- **Programmatic writes are gone**: `option.value`, `viewValue`, `disabled`, `showCheckbox` and `KbqTimezoneOption.timezone` are bound in the template.
- **`KbqOptgroup.disabled` and `KbqOptionActionComponent.disabled` are signals**: `group.disabled()`.
- **`KbqOption.stateChanges` no longer emits for `disabled`**, and `textElement` is typed `ElementRef | undefined`.

`option-signals` rewrites the reads of the group and the action, and reports the writes:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:option-signals --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Number input and input type
sections.body:
`KbqNumberInput.value`, `KbqNumberInput.disabled` and `KbqInput.type` are signal inputs read through a getter: a read is unchanged, a programmatic write no longer compiles. Bind `[value]`, `[disabled]` and `[type]`, or write through the form control. `input-signals` reports every write:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:input-signals --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: List
sections.body:
The inputs of `KbqListSelection` and `KbqListOption` are signal inputs read through a getter: a read is unchanged, a programmatic write no longer compiles. Bind them in the template, and disable the list through its form control. `KbqListOption.selected` and `KbqListSelection.multipleMode` stay writable. `list-signals` reports every write:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:list-signals --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Checkbox, toggle, radio, button toggle, buttons, icons, search and pop-ups
sections.body:
Their inputs are signal inputs named `<member>Input`, handed to the unchanged member from `ngOnChanges`: reading and writing `checkbox.checked`, `button.disabled`, `icon.iconName` or `tooltip.content` works as before. The same goes for the tooltip, popover, popover confirm, app switcher and notification center triggers, the password toggle and the ellipsis center, and for the tags, file uploads, accordion item, navbar item, notification item and sidebar. The exception is a member another migration moved to a signal, such as `color` (see Color as a signal) or the tag members and the form-field state of the tag list (see Tags).

- **A subclass** that implements `ngOnChanges` calls `super.ngOnChanges(changes)`, and one that redeclared an `@Input()` overrides the `<member>Input` signal input instead, e.g. `iconNameInput`.
- **A boolean input** accepts `boolean | string | null | undefined` in a template, rather than anything.
- **`KbqPopUp.elementRef` is a protected getter.** A panel that renders an element of its own overrides it over a `viewChild()` instead of re-declaring the field with `@ViewChild`.

`signal-inputs-subclasses` reports every subclass:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:signal-inputs-subclasses --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Datepicker
sections.body:
The inputs of `KbqDatepicker`, `KbqDatepickerInput`, `KbqDatepickerToggleIconComponent`, `KbqCalendar`, `KbqCalendarHeader` and `KbqMonthView` are signal inputs named `<member>Input`, handed to the unchanged member from `ngOnChanges`: reading and writing `datepicker.opened`, `datepicker.startAt`, `input.min` or `calendar.minDate` works as before. The exception is the form-field state of `KbqDatepickerInput`: `value`, `id`, `placeholder`, `focused`, `empty`, `required`, `disabled` and `errorState` are signals, migrated by `form-field-signals` (see Form field review (21.0.0)).

- **A subclass** that implements `ngOnChanges` marks it `override` and calls `super.ngOnChanges(changes)`, and one that redeclared an `@Input()` overrides the `<member>Input` signal input instead, e.g. `minInput`.
- **A `SimpleChanges` passed to `ngOnChanges` by hand** is keyed by the `<member>Input` names: `minDateInput`, not `minDate`.
- **A boolean input** — `hasBackdrop`, `disabled` and `opened` — accepts `boolean | string | null | undefined` in a template.

`datepicker-signals` reports every subclass and every direct call of `ngOnChanges`:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:datepicker-signals --project "<your project>"
```

**Without a locale service, the placeholder names the format the input takes.** It used to be the `ru-RU` one whatever locale the date adapter parsed in. It now follows the date adapter of the input — `KBQ_DATE_LOCALE`, Angular's `LOCALE_ID` unless provided, on a component too — so with the default `en-US` it reads `yyyy-mm-dd`; for a locale the library ships no strings for, or a format set through `KBQ_DATE_FORMATS`, it is the format itself, such as `yyyy/mm/dd`. To keep the former one, bind `[placeholder]` or pass it to `kbqDatepickerLocaleConfigurationProvider()`. With a locale service nothing changes.

sections.heading: Tabs
sections.body:
The inputs of `KbqTabGroup`, `KbqTab`, `KbqTabNavBar`, `KbqTabLink` and of the header, labels and bodies inside the tab group are signal inputs named `<member>Input`, handed to the unchanged member from `ngOnChanges`: reading and writing `tabGroup.selectedIndex`, `tabGroup.headerPosition`, `tab.disabled` or `tabLink.active` works as before. Their queries are signal queries behind getters: `KbqTabGroup.tabs` and `KbqTabNavBar.items` are still `QueryList`s whose `changes` emit as before.

- **A subclass** that implements `ngOnChanges` marks it `override` and calls `super.ngOnChanges(changes)`, and one that redeclared an `@Input()` overrides the `<member>Input` signal input instead, e.g. `headerPositionInput`. A query it redeclared with `@ContentChildren` or `@ViewChild` — `tabs`, `items`, `templateLabel` — is overridden as a getter.
- **A `SimpleChanges` passed to `ngOnChanges` by hand** is keyed by the `<member>Input` names: `disabledInput`, not `disabled`.
- **A boolean input** — `disabled`, `active`, `vertical`, `disablePagination` — accepts `boolean | string | null | undefined` in a template.
- **A bound `undefined`** resets the member to its default rather than leaving it as it was: `headerPosition` becomes `'above'`, `animationDuration` the duration of `KBQ_TABS_CONFIG`, `tooltipTitle` `''` and a boolean input `false`, `selectedIndex` selects the first enabled tab, and a `KbqTabLink` gets `tabIndex` `0` and its generated `id`.
- **`KbqTab.templateLabel` follows the `kbqTabLabel` in the content of the tab**: once that is removed, the tab shows its text label rather than the removed template.

`tabs-signals-and-aria` reports every subclass and every direct call of `ngOnChanges`:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:tabs-signals-and-aria --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Query lists
sections.body:
The `options` of `KbqSelect`, `KbqAutocomplete` and `KbqListSelection`, the `tags` of `KbqSelect` and `KbqTagList`, `KbqRadioGroup.radios`, `KbqTreeSelection.unorderedOptions`, the `focusableItems` of `KbqNavbar` and `KbqVerticalNavbar`, and the `textElement` of `KbqTag` and `KbqDropdownItem` are getters over signal queries. They keep their types — a `QueryList` whose `changes` emit as before, or an `ElementRef` — so reading them works as before. Before the content is initialized a `QueryList` is empty rather than `undefined`.

- **A subclass** that redeclared one of them, with a query decorator or as a field, removes the redeclaration or overrides the getter.
- **A write** to one of them no longer compiles: render the items in the template.
- **`KbqCodeBlock.tabLinkTemplate`**, which is protected, is a signal: a subclass reads `this.tabLinkTemplate()`.

`query-list-signals` reports every redeclaration and write:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:query-list-signals --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: State as signals
sections.body:
The state that components and services expose for reading is a signal, where it used to be a `BehaviorSubject`, an `Observable` or a plain field. The streams that report events stay observables.

| Member                                                                                                                    | Was                                   | Now                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `silentMode`, `loadingMode`, `errorMode`, `loadingMore`, `loadMoreErrorMode`, `hasMore` of `KbqNotificationCenterService` | `BehaviorSubject<boolean>`            | `Signal<boolean>`, written by the `set…()` methods |
| `unreadItemsCounter` of `KbqNotificationCenterService` and `KbqNotificationCenterTrigger`                                 | `Observable<string>`                  | `Signal<string>`                                   |
| `KbqNotificationCenterService.groupedItems`                                                                               | `Observable<KbqNotificationsGroup[]>` | `Signal<KbqNotificationsGroup[]>`                  |
| `hovered`, `focused` of `KbqToastService` and `KbqToastComponent`                                                         | `BehaviorSubject<boolean>`            | `Signal<boolean>`                                  |
| `filteredOptions` of `KbqFilters`, `KbqPipeSelectComponent` and `KbqPipeMultiSelectComponent`                             | `Observable`                          | a read-only `Signal`                               |
| `KbqSelect.hiddenItems`                                                                                                   | `number`                              | `Signal<number>`, as in `KbqTreeSelect`            |
| `KbqSearchExpandable.value`                                                                                               | `BehaviorSubject<string>`             | `WritableSignal<string>`                           |
| `hovered` of `KbqPopUp` and `KbqPopUpTrigger`: tooltips, popovers, the notification center and the app switcher           | `BehaviorSubject<boolean>`            | `Signal<boolean>`                                  |

- **Read** them with a call — `service.silentMode()`, `trigger.unreadItemsCounter()` — instead of `.value`, `.getValue()` or `| async`. Where a stream is still needed, wrap the signal in `toObservable()` from `@angular/core/rxjs-interop`.
- **Write** the notification center flags with their `set…()` methods and the search value with `value.set()`; the other signals are read-only.
- **`KbqNotificationCenterService.changes`** no longer emits on subscription: a handler that relied on that runs once on its own before subscribing.
- **`KbqFilters.filteredOptions`** now follows a change of the `filters` input too.
- **A pop-up trigger no longer marks its host view for check** when it opens or closes: an OnPush view that renders a field of its own, written from a `visibleChange` subscription made in code, calls `markForCheck()` itself or keeps the field in a signal. An output bound in the template needs nothing.
- **A getter backed by a signal is a tracked read.** `isOpen` of the pop-up triggers, `opened` of `KbqDropdownTrigger`, `KbqDatepicker` and `KbqSidebar`, `panelOpen` of `KbqSelect`, `KbqTreeSelect` and `KbqAutocompleteTrigger`, `expanded` of `KbqAccordionItem`, `isOpened` of `KbqSearchExpandable`, `selected` of the options, `selectedIndex` of `KbqTabGroup` and `isActive` of `KbqTab` keep their type, but reading one inside an `effect()` or a `computed()` makes it follow that state: an effect that opens or closes a component depending on one reads it with `untracked()`. The commands of the components — `open()`, `close()`, `toggle()`, `select()`, `writeValue()` and the like — read nothing an effect calling them would follow.
- **A number input bound to `undefined` or `null`** falls back to its default instead of becoming `NaN`: `tabIndex` of `kbq-checkbox`, `kbq-toggle`, `kbq-radio-button`, `kbq-search-expandable` and `kbqTabLink` reads `0` (a tab link no longer renders `tabindex="NaN"`), `selectedIndex` of `kbq-tab-group` selects the first enabled tab, `offset` of `kbqAppSwitcher` takes the default offset, and `tabIndex` of `kbq-list-selection` and `kbq-tree-selection` gives back the default tab stop (`0`, or `-1` without options). A value that is not a finite number counts the same.
- **Tabbing out of a list, tag list or tree leaves `tabIndex` alone.** `kbq-list-selection`, `kbq-tag-list` and `kbq-tree-selection` take themselves out of the tab order in the DOM only, so `tabIndex` reads the same value while the focus leaves, and then put back the tab stop they render. A tag list with a tag input renders no `tabindex` again instead of keeping `-1`, and a tree keeps a bound `[tabIndex]` when its rendered nodes change.
- **A subclass** of `KbqToastComponent`, `KbqPopUp` or `KbqPopUpTrigger` sets its hover state with the protected `setHovered()`; one of `KbqPipeSelectComponent` drops its `super.ngOnInit()` call, and one of `KbqDatepickerToggleIconComponent` its `super.ngAfterContentInit()` and `super.ngOnDestroy()` calls, since the classes no longer implement them. The protected `isListMode`, `showStartCalendar` and `showEndCalendar` of the date pipes are signals, `returnButton` may be `undefined` (the back button renders only when the pipe template has `values`), and a date pipe template binds `(keydown.tab)` and `(keydown.shift.tab)` of its date inputs to `onDateInputTab()`, which hides the calendars before the browser moves the focus.
- **`KbqFileItem`** keeps its `loading` and `progress` subjects, which the application updates.

`v21-upgrade` reports these reads, writes and `super` calls:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:v21-upgrade --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: Deprecated API removal (21.0.0)
sections.body: The APIs deprecated in 20.x are removed in 21.0.0, those whose note promised removal in the next major release and those deprecated without a date alike. A renamed member or alias is rewritten by `v21-upgrade`; for the rest it reports the file and the replacement to use.

sections.heading: Accordion
sections.body:
| Removed                                   | Use instead                                                                             | Migration |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| the `kbq-accordion-trigger__action` class | a `kbq-accordion-header__actions` element next to the trigger in `kbq-accordion-header` | reported  |

An action inside the trigger is a focusable element inside a `role="button"`, so the actions move out of the trigger: see [Interactive elements](/en/components/accordion/overview#interactive-elements). `v21-upgrade` reports the class in templates, style sheets and code.

sections.heading: Code block and icon button
sections.body:
| Removed                                         | Use instead                       | Migration |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------- |
| `canLoad` on `<kbq-code-block>`                 | `canDownload`                     | rewritten |
| `codeFiles` on `<kbq-code-block>`               | `files`                           | rewritten |
| `KbqCodeBlock.canLoadInput` / `.codeFilesInput` | `canDownload()` / `files()`       | reported  |
| `KbqCodeBlock.scrollableCodeContent`            | `scrollTo(options)`               | reported  |
| `small` on an icon button                       | `size="compact"`                  | rewritten |
| the `kbq-icon-button_small` class               | `kbq-icon-button_compact`         | rewritten |
| `KbqIconButton.small`                           | `size` (`'compact'` / `'normal'`) | reported  |

The aliases no longer fill in for their replacements: a `<kbq-code-block>` that binds both `canLoad` and `canDownload`, or both `codeFiles` and `files`, is reported and has to merge each pair into one binding. So is one that binds `canDownload` or `files` twice, which is what the 20.0.0 migration made of such a pair: only the last binding takes effect. A bound `[small]="expr"` becomes `[size]="(expr) ? 'compact' : 'normal'"`. A valueless `small` never took effect, because the input had no boolean transform; it is reported, as is a static `small` with any other value than `"true"`, which made the button compact.

sections.heading: Core
sections.body:
| Removed                                | Use instead                                                                | Migration           |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `KbqThemeSelector.Default`             | `KbqThemeSelector.Light`                                                   | rewritten           |
| `KbqThemeNames.Default`                | `KbqThemeNames.Light`                                                      | rewritten           |
| `KbqDefaultThemes`                     | `KBQ_DEFAULT_THEMES`                                                       | rewritten           |
| `KbqTheme`                             | `KbqThemeConfig`: `colorScheme` is required, `selected` is gone            | rewritten, reported |
| `ThemeService`                         | `KbqThemeService`                                                          | reported            |
| `ThemeService.current` / `.getTheme()` | `currentTheme()`, a signal                                                 | reported            |
| `ThemeService.themes`                  | `themes()` / `setThemes()`                                                 | reported            |
| `ThemeService.setTheme(theme)`         | `setMode(theme.colorScheme)`, or `selectTheme(theme.name)` to pin a theme  | reported            |
| `getOptionScrollPosition()`            | `KbqOption.focus()` or `kbqFocusAndReveal(element)`: both scroll into view | reported            |

`v21-upgrade` reports `ThemeService` and `getOptionScrollPosition` where they are imported from `@koobiq/components/core`, and every file that names `KbqTheme`. Give each custom theme its `colorScheme` and compare a theme with `currentTheme()` instead of reading `selected`. Unlike `ThemeService`, `KbqThemeService` applies a theme as soon as it is injected and starts in `'auto'` mode: an app that called `setTheme()` at startup to force a theme sets `kbqThemeProvider({ mode: 'light' })` instead. The rest of the service is described in the theme service review below.

sections.heading: Dropdown and select
sections.body:
| Removed                                                             | Use instead                                                                               | Migration |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `KbqDropdown.triggerWidth`, `KbqDropdownPanel.triggerWidth`         | `KbqDropdownTrigger.widthOrigin`, to match the panel to an element other than the trigger | reported  |
| `offsetY` of `KbqSelect`, `KbqTreeSelect`, `KbqTimezoneSelect`      | the `--kbq-connected-overlay-gap` CSS variable, set on `:root` or on the overlay pane     | reported  |
| `AUTOCOMPLETE_PANEL_HEIGHT`                                         | a constant of your own: the panel is capped by `--kbq-autocomplete-size-panel-max-height` | reported  |
| `DropdownPositionX` / `DropdownPositionY`                           | `KbqDropdownPositionX` / `KbqDropdownPositionY`                                           | rewritten |
| `KbqSelectPanelWidth`, `KbqTreeSelectPanelWidth`                    | `KbqPanelWidth` from `@koobiq/components/core`                                            | rewritten |
| `clearValue()` of `KbqSelect`, `KbqTreeSelect`, `KbqTimezoneSelect` | a projected `<kbq-cleaner />`; from code, reset the bound form control                    | reported  |
| the `kbq-dropdown__group-header_small` class                        | `<kbq-optgroup label="…" />`, `KbqOptgroup` from `@koobiq/components/core`                | reported  |

None of the removed members was an input, so no template binds them, and of `triggerWidth`, `offsetY` and `AUTOCOMPLETE_PANEL_HEIGHT` only `offsetY` of `kbq-timezone-select` still had an effect: it moved the panel. `v21-upgrade` reports `.triggerWidth` in a file that uses the dropdown, `triggerWidth` in a `KbqDropdownPanel` implementation, `.offsetY` in a file that uses one of the selects and an `offsetY` field of their subclass; the `offsetY` input of `KbqDropdownTrigger` stays. It renames the position types in a file that names `@koobiq/components/dropdown` and moves the panel width types to the core import; the position types elsewhere, an aliased import and a re-export are reported. `.clearValue` is reported in a file that uses one of the selects, except on `this` and on a form field, whose `clearValue()` stays; like the cleaner, it spared the options `clearPredicate` keeps, while a reset control loses them all. `<kbq-optgroup>` renders the subheading of the removed modifier inside a dropdown; `kbq-dropdown__group-header` itself stays.

sections.heading: Filter bar
sections.body:
| Removed                               | Use instead                                                                                            | Migration                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `KbqFilterBarRefresher`               | `KbqFilterRefresher`                                                                                   | rewritten                    |
| `KbqFilterBar.changes`                | `filter()` read in an `effect()`, or the `(filterChange)` output: `changes` never emitted              | reported                     |
| `KbqPipeMinWidth` (`kbqPipeMinWidth`) | nothing: a pipe lays its name and value out as shrinkable grid tracks, which keeps a short part intact | removed; other uses reported |
| `KbqPipe.required`                    | `cleanable: false` and `removable: false`: the filter bar never read `required`                        | reported                     |

`v21-upgrade` reports `.changes` in a file that names `KbqFilterBar`. It removes `KbqPipeMinWidth` from the `@koobiq/components/filter-bar` import and from `imports` arrays and the `kbqPipeMinWidth` attribute from templates, and reports any other reference to the directive. It reports a read of `data.required` in a custom pipe, and a `required` key only in an object literal that also has `cleanable`, `removable` or `type: KbqPipeTypes.…`: the `required` of a form config or a validator in the same file is left alone.

sections.heading: Form field
sections.body:
| Removed                                                        | Use instead                                                                         | Migration |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `KbqPasswordHint` (`<kbq-password-hint>`)                      | `KbqReactivePasswordHint` (`<kbq-reactive-password-hint [hasError]="…">`)           | reported  |
| `PasswordRules`                                                | `PasswordValidators` from `@koobiq/components/core`, or a `ValidatorFn` of your own | reported  |
| `regExpPasswordValidator`                                      | `Validators.pattern` or a `ValidatorFn` of your own                                 | reported  |
| `hasPasswordStrengthError()`                                   | the errors of the form control                                                      | reported  |
| the `passwordStrength` error the form field set on the control | the errors of the password validators                                               | reported  |
| `KbqFormField.passwordHints` / `.hasPasswordHint`              | `viewChildren(KbqReactivePasswordHint)`                                             | reported  |
| `KbqInputPassword.checkRules()` / `.checkRule`                 | `control.updateValueAndValidity()` after changing the validators                    | reported  |
| `KbqFormField.canCleanerClearByEsc`                            | nothing: it was unused                                                              | reported  |
| `KbqFormField.onKeyDown()`                                     | nothing: it was a no-op                                                             | reported  |
| `KbqStepper.connectTo()`                                       | nothing: the stepper finds the number input of its form field by itself             | reported  |

`KbqReactivePasswordHint` shows the state it is given: put each rule on the form control as a validator and bind `[hasError]` to its error, for example `control.hasError('minLength')`. It has no counterpart of `[rule]`, `[min]`, `[max]`, `[regex]`, `[checkRule]` or `[viewFormField]`, so place it inside the `kbq-form-field`, which links it to the control through `aria-describedby`. `v21-upgrade` reports the first four where they are imported from `@koobiq/components/form-field`, `<kbq-password-hint>` and its classes in templates and style sheets, a check of the `passwordStrength` error, `.passwordHints`, `.hasPasswordHint` and `.onKeyDown()` on a form field, every `canCleanerClearByEsc`, `checkRules()` in a file that uses `KbqInputPassword`, and `connectTo()` in a file that uses `KbqStepper`.

sections.heading: Checkbox and toggle
sections.body:
`KbqCheckbox` and `KbqToggleComponent` no longer implement `ControlValueAccessor`. The `KbqCheckable` host directive has been the value accessor of both, so forms never called their own members; `[(ngModel)]` and `[formControl]` work as before.

| Removed                                                   | Use instead                                   | Migration |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `KbqCheckbox` / `KbqToggleComponent.writeValue()`         | `checked = !!value`                           | reported  |
| `.setDisabledState()` of both                             | `disabled = isDisabled`                       | reported  |
| `.registerOnChange()` of both                             | the `(change)` output                         | reported  |
| `.registerOnTouched()` of both                            | the `touched` state of the bound form control | reported  |
| `KbqCheckbox.onTouched`                                   | nothing: it was never called                  | reported  |
| `KBQ_CHECKBOX_CONTROL_VALUE_ACCESSOR`                     | nothing: `KbqCheckable` registers itself      | reported  |
| `TransitionCheckState` from `@koobiq/components/checkbox` | the same enum from `@koobiq/components/core`  | rewritten |

`v21-upgrade` reports these uses in a file that names either class or its tag, except calls on `this`. A call that has to stay can go to the host directive: `viewChild(KbqCheckbox, { read: KbqCheckable })`, with `KbqCheckable` from `@koobiq/components/core`. It moves `TransitionCheckState` from the checkbox import into the core one, and reports it imported under an alias, re-exported or read through a namespace import of the checkbox.

`KbqToggleComponent.onLabelTextChange()` does nothing now and is deprecated for removal in 22.0.0: delete the call. `v21-upgrade` reports it.

The protected `KbqToggleComponent.currentCheckState` is a `Signal` shared with the host `KbqCheckable`: a subclass reads it as `currentCheckState()` and changes it through the `checked` and `indeterminate` setters. `v21-upgrade` reports a read without the call in a subclass.

sections.heading: Navbar, ellipsis center and description list
sections.body:
| Removed                                   | Use instead                                                                                                     | Migration         |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `longTitle` on `kbq-navbar-brand`         | nothing: the brand switches to the two-line title when the title does not fit on one line                       | removed, reported |
| `KbqNavbarBrand.longTitle` in code        | nothing                                                                                                         | reported          |
| `KbqNavbarItem.getTitleWidth()`           | `getOuterElementWidth()` of the item's `KbqNavbarTitle`; the navbar itself collapses by `getCollapsibleWidth()` | reported          |
| `KbqNavbarTitle.outerElementWidth`        | `getOuterElementWidth()`                                                                                        | reported          |
| `KbqEllipsisCenterDirective.resizeStream` | nothing: the shared `ResizeObserver` re-measures the host                                                       | reported          |
| `minWidth` on `<kbq-dl>`                  | `verticalBreakpoint`                                                                                            | rewritten         |
| `KbqDlComponent.minWidth` in code         | `verticalBreakpoint()`                                                                                          | reported          |

`[longTitle]="true"` forced the compact title on a name that fits and `false` kept the default one for a name that does not; neither has a replacement. `outerElementWidth` held the width measured once on init and only fed `getTitleWidth()`. `minWidth` took precedence over `verticalBreakpoint`, so a `<kbq-dl>` that sets both keeps its `minWidth` and is reported: move the value into `verticalBreakpoint`. A `[minWidth]` that resolved to `null` or `undefined` left the decision to `verticalBreakpoint`, while `[verticalBreakpoint]` given such a value never switches to the vertical layout, so bind a number. `v21-upgrade` reports each renamed `minWidth` whose value is not a number literal.

sections.heading: Popover trigger
sections.body:
The trigger inputs without the `kbqPopover` prefix are removed from `KbqPopoverTrigger` and `KbqPopoverConfirmTrigger`. The members they set — `defaultPaddings`, `container`, `hasBackdrop`, `hasCloseButton`, `closeOnScroll` and `backdropClass` — stay public, so code that reads or writes them keeps compiling.

| Removed                                          | Use instead                                                 | Migration |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| the `hideIfNotInViewPort` input                  | `kbqPopoverHideIfNotInViewPort`                             | rewritten |
| the `defaultPaddings` input                      | `kbqPopoverDefaultPaddings`                                 | rewritten |
| the `container` input                            | `kbqPopoverContainer`                                       | rewritten |
| the `hasBackdrop` input                          | `kbqPopoverHasBackdrop`                                     | rewritten |
| the `hasCloseButton` input                       | `kbqPopoverHasCloseButton`                                  | rewritten |
| the `closeOnScroll` input                        | `kbqPopoverCloseOnScroll`                                   | rewritten |
| the `backdropClass` input                        | `kbqPopoverBackdropClass`                                   | rewritten |
| `KbqPopoverTrigger.hideIfNotInViewPort` (signal) | `popoverHideIfNotInViewPort()`                              | reported  |
| `getKbqPopoverInvalidPositionError()`            | nothing: an invalid placement warns and falls back to `top` | reported  |

`v21-upgrade` rewrites bindings, static and valueless attributes only on an element that carries `kbqPopover` or `kbqPopoverConfirm`: other components, such as the dropdown and the select, have inputs of the same names. It reports a `hostDirectives` entry of `KbqPopoverTrigger` that exposes a removed input; expose the prefixed one instead, for example `'kbqPopoverHasBackdrop: hasBackdrop'`.

sections.heading: Styles and theming
sections.body:
| Removed                                                                                                     | Use instead                                                                                                  | Migration                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| the arguments of `koobiq-theme()`, `koobiq-typography()` and `kbq-core-theme()`                             | nothing: they were ignored                                                                                   | removed; with nested `()` reported |
| `kbq-contrast()`, `kbq-palette()`, `kbq-color()`                                                            | the CSS variables of the theme, for example `var(--kbq-foreground-contrast)`                                 | reported                           |
| `kbq-typography-config()`                                                                                   | the `--kbq-typography-*` CSS variables                                                                       | reported                           |
| `@koobiq/components/core/styles/tokens`                                                                     | the modules it forwarded: `@koobiq/design-tokens/web/variables`, `palette`, `typography` and `md-typography` | reported                           |
| `prebuilt-themes/light-theme.css`, `prebuilt-themes/dark-theme.css`                                         | `prebuilt-themes/theme.css`                                                                                  | rewritten                          |
| the `md-h1`…`md-h6`, `md-body`, `md-body-mono`, `md-caption`, `md-table-cell` and `md-table-header` classes | the `kbq-md-` class of the same name, for example `kbq-md-h1`                                                | rewritten, reported                |

The light and dark files were copies of `theme.css`, which holds both themes. `v21-upgrade` rewrites them in style sheets, code, templates and the `styles` of `angular.json`, and keeps a single `theme.css` where both were loaded. A theme map built only to pass to `koobiq-theme()`, such as `kbq-light-theme($tokens)`, can go along with the argument: `kbq-light-theme()` and `kbq-dark-theme()` are deprecated and will be removed in 22.0.0, since nothing in the library reads their map. Read the CSS variables of the theme instead, for example `var(--kbq-foreground-contrast)`; the migration reports both functions. The markdown classes are rewritten in `class` attributes, `[class.…]` bindings and selectors; in any other string, such as `classList.add('md-h1')` or `[ngClass]`, they are reported.

sections.heading: Tag input
sections.body:
Validation belongs to the `<kbq-tag-list>` control, so the validation members of the tag input are removed. A `[formControl]` or `[ngModel]` bound to `<input kbqTagInputFor>` keeps working: `kbqAutocomplete` drives the input through it.

| Removed                           | Use instead                                                                   | Migration |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `KbqTagInput.ngControl`           | the control you bound to the input                                            | reported  |
| `KbqTagInput.triggerValidation()` | nothing: it was a no-op, and the tag list control revalidates on every change | reported  |
| `KbqTagTextControl.ngControl`     | nothing: the library never read it                                            | —         |

`v21-upgrade` reports these uses in a file that names `KbqTagInput` or binds its `exportAs`, except on `this`, and a subclass of `KbqTagInput` that mentions either member. `KbqTagTextControl` is not exported, and a control passed to `KbqTagList.registerInput()` that still declares `ngControl` keeps compiling: the member was optional.

sections.heading: Toast container
sections.body:
| Removed                                          | Use instead                                                               | Migration |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `--kbq-toast-stack-size-margin-top`              | `--kbq-toast-stack-size-margin-vertical`                                  | rewritten |
| `--kbq-toast-stack-size-margin-right`            | `--kbq-toast-stack-size-margin-horizontal`                                | rewritten |
| `KbqToastContainerComponent.dispatchScrollEvent` | nothing: the container reports its own reflow through `elementScrolled()` | reported  |

The removed properties already set both edges: `-top` also set the bottom margin of a stack at the bottom, and `-right` the left margin of a stack on the left. `v21-upgrade` renames them in style sheets, templates and code, and reports a file that declares both a removed and a new name: the new one used to win, after the rename the cascade decides.

sections.heading: Tree option
sections.body:
| Removed                                                      | Use instead                                    | Migration |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `KbqTreeOptionChange.isUserInput`                            | nothing: the tree never set it, it was `false` | reported  |
| the second argument of the `KbqTreeOptionChange` constructor | nothing: `new KbqTreeOptionChange(option)`     | reported  |

A check of `isUserInput` on a tree option change never passed: delete it with the branch it guarded. `v21-upgrade` reports `.isUserInput` in a file that names `KbqTreeOptionChange`, `$event.isUserInput` bound to an output of `<kbq-tree-option>`, and a second argument passed to the constructor or to `super()` in a subclass. The `isUserInput` of `KbqOptionSelectionChange` and of `KbqTreeSelectChange` stays.

| Deprecated, removed in 22.0.0                     | Use instead                                                     | Migration |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `(onSelectAll)` on `<kbq-tree-selection>`         | `(selectAllChange)`                                             | rewritten |
| `(onCopy)` on `<kbq-tree-selection>`              | `(copyChange)`                                                  | rewritten |
| `(onSelectionChange)` on `<kbq-tree-option>`      | `(selectionChange)`                                             | rewritten |
| `KbqTreeSelection.onSelectAll`, `.onCopy` in code | `selectAllChange`, `copyChange`                                 | reported  |
| `KbqTreeOption.onSelectionChange` in code         | `selectionChange`                                               | reported  |
| `KbqTreeNode.mostRecentTreeNode`                  | a query of the nodes, for example `viewChildren(KbqTreeOption)` | reported  |

The replacements emit the same events. The `onSelectAll` and `onCopy` outputs of `kbq-list-selection` and the `onSelectAll` output of `kbq-tree-select` are not deprecated and stay.

sections.heading: Running the migration
sections.body:
`v21-upgrade` is registered for 21.0.0, so an `ng update` to that version runs it:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:v21-upgrade --project "<your project>"
```

With `--fix false` it only reports what it would change.

sections.heading: ThemePalette removal (21.0.0)
sections.body:
`ThemePalette` is removed from `@koobiq/components/core`: `KbqComponentColors` describes the colors the components support.

| Removed                                                   | Use instead                                                          | Migration |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `ThemePalette.Error`, `.Warning`, `.Success`              | `KbqComponentColors.Error`, `.Warning`, `.Success`                   | rewritten |
| `ThemePalette.Primary`, `.Secondary`, `.Info`, `.Default` | no color, or a member of `KbqComponentColors` the component supports | reported  |
| `ThemePalette.Empty`                                      | an unset `color`                                                     | reported  |
| the `ThemePalette` type                                   | `KbqComponentColors`                                                 | reported  |

`Error`, `Warning` and `Success` have the same values in both enums, so the rewrite changes nothing on screen. `Primary`, `Secondary` (`Default` is its alias) and `Info` set a `kbq-primary`, `kbq-secondary` or `kbq-info` class that no component styles, so such a component was drawn without its color rules; without a color it takes its default one. `Empty` is `''`, which also falls back to the default color, while `KbqComponentColors.Empty` is `'empty'`, a color of its own: do not swap one for the other.

`v21-upgrade` rewrites the three members and drops the `ThemePalette` import once nothing else names it. It reports every other use in a file that imports `ThemePalette` from `@koobiq/components/core`, including a field that hands the enum to a template. A re-export of `ThemePalette` from `@koobiq/components/core` is left as is and reported: `KbqComponentColors` has other members and values, so re-export it under its own name and migrate the files that import `ThemePalette` through it.

sections.heading: Unused core API removal (21.0.0)
sections.body:
`@koobiq/components/core` drops the undocumented exports, members and Sass that nothing in the library used. They were never deprecated: most are leftovers of removed features or implementation details that leaked into the public API.

| Removed                                                                                                            | Use instead                                                                                                                                                                                            | Migration |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| `POSITION_MAP`, `EXTENDED_OVERLAY_POSITIONS`, `POSITION_PRIORITY_STRATEGY`, the twelve `*_POSITION_PRIORITY` lists | `kbqPlacement` on the trigger; copy a value you need                                                                                                                                                   | reported  |
| `ARROW_BOTTOM_MARGIN_AND_HALF_HEIGHT`, `SELECT_PANEL_VIEWPORT_PADDING`, `NUMBER_FORMAT_REGEXP`, `isWithin()`       | a value or function of your own                                                                                                                                                                        | reported  |
| `KBQ_SELECT_SCROLL_STRATEGY_PROVIDER`                                                                              | nothing: `KBQ_SELECT_SCROLL_STRATEGY` has a root default; provide the token itself to change it                                                                                                        | reported  |
| `KBQ_CHECKABLE_CONTROL_VALUE_ACCESSOR`                                                                             | nothing: `KbqCheckable` registers itself                                                                                                                                                               | reported  |
| `KbqHover`                                                                                                         | `(mouseenter)` and `(mouseleave)`, or `:hover`                                                                                                                                                         | reported  |
| `CanColor`                                                                                                         | `Signal`, or `KbqColorDirective`                                                                                                                                         | reported  |
| `KbqAnimationCurves`, `KbqAnimationDurations`                                                                      | constants of your own: the library animates in CSS                                                                                                                                                     | reported  |
| `KbqRectangleItem`, `countGroupLabelsBeforeOption()`                                                               | no replacement                                                                                                                                                                                         | reported  |
| `KbqPopUp.markForCheck()`                                                                                          | nothing after `updateClassMap()` or a change of `visibility`, which re-render the pop-up; for another field, `changeDetectorRef.markForCheck()` in a subclass, `instance.detectChanges()` in a trigger | reported  |
| `KbqPopUp.warning`, `.handleBodyInteraction()`, the protected `closeOnInteraction`                                 | no replacement: `warning` did nothing, nothing called `handleBodyInteraction()`, and `closeOnInteraction` only gated it                                                                                | reported  |
| `KbqDecimalPipe.isSpecialFormatForRULocale()`, `KbqRoundDecimalPipe.roundingOptions`                               | private now: the pipe arguments and the formatters locale configuration                                                                                                                                | reported  |
| `KbqFormElement.isRow`                                                                                             | the `kbq-form__row` class of the element                                                                                                                                                               | reported  |
| `KbqLineSetter` and the `kbq-2-line`, `kbq-3-line`, `kbq-multi-line` classes of a list item                        | nothing: no style read them                                                                                                                                                                            | reported  |
| `KbqLine`, `KbqListItem.lines`                                                                                     | nothing: only `lines` read `KbqLine`, and nothing counted the lines; the `kbq-line` attribute still places an element in the text of a list item                                                       | reported  |
| `KbqSelectSearch.hasPlaceholder()`                                                                                 | the placeholder of the search input                                                                                                                                                                    | reported  |
| the `mcListIcon` attribute of a list item                                                                          | `kbq-list-icon`                                                                                                                                                                                        | rewritten |
| the `mcLine` attribute                                                                                             | `kbq-line`                                                                                                                                                                                             | rewritten |

The Sass that goes is reachable only through a deep import, since `@koobiq/components` forwards none of it:

- the modules `core/styles/functions` (its index, `number` and `string`), `typography/typography-utils`, `common/clearfix` and `common/popup`;
- `kbq-markdown-typography-config()`, the `typography-utils` getters (`kbq-typography-level()`, `kbq-font-size()`…), `popup-params`, `input-placeholder`, `rtl-value()` and `kbq-typography-css-variables`;
- the timing variables of `core/styles/functions/timing` but `$ease-out-circ`, `$ease-in-out-quad` and `$ease-in-out-circ`.

For typography, use the `--kbq-typography-*` CSS variables or `kbq-typography-level-to-styles-css-variables()` of `core/styles/common/tokens`; copy anything else into your own styles. `v21-upgrade` reports each load and use. The compiled CSS also loses a few prefixes for browsers the library does not support: `-ms-text-size-adjust`, `-ms-overflow-style`, `-moz-` and `-ms-user-select`, the old flexbox `display` values and an `@-moz-document` copy of `.layout-fill`.

sections.heading: Deprecated for removal in 22.0.0
sections.body:
The documented core API that has a replacement is deprecated instead; `v21-upgrade` reports each use:

| Deprecated                                                                                                       | Use instead                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the unprefixed date pipes (`absoluteLongDate`…`durationShort`), their `ImpurePipe` twins and `BaseFormatterPipe` | the `kbq*` pipe of the same format with the same arguments, for example `kbqAbsoluteLongDate`: it follows a locale change |
| the `mcHighlight` pipe (`KbqHighlightPipe`)                                                                      | `kbqHighlightBold` (`KbqHighlightBoldPipe`)                                                                               |
| `isDigit()`                                                                                                      | `isNumberKey()`                                                                                                           |
| `isBoolean()`                                                                                                    | `typeof value === 'boolean'`                                                                                              |
| `KbqMeasureScrollbarService`                                                                                     | `element.offsetWidth - element.clientWidth` of the element that scrolls                                                   |
| `FocusKeyManager.getFocusOrigin()`                                                                               | the origin passed to `setFocusOrigin()`                                                                                   |
| `dateInput` of the datepicker locale configuration                                                               | `KBQ_DATE_FORMATS`: nothing reads `dateInput`                                                                             |

sections.heading: Unused component API removal (21.0.0)
sections.body:
The component entry points drop the exports, members and styles that nothing in the library used. They were never deprecated: most are leftovers of removed features or implementation details that leaked into the public API. `v21-upgrade` reports each use.

| Removed                                                                     | Use instead                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `normalizeSplitter()`, `isInt()`, `isDigit()` of `@koobiq/components/input` | `value.replace(/,/g, '.')`, `/^-?\d+$/.test(value)`; `isFloat()` stays                                 |
| `KbqTimeRangeTranslateTypeMap`                                              | `Record<KbqTimeRangeType, KbqTimeRangeTranslationType>`                                                |
| `KbqTabBodyOriginState`                                                     | `'left' \| 'right'`                                                                                    |
| `KbqDatepickerIntl`                                                         | nothing: no view rendered its labels; the texts come from `kbqDatepickerLocaleConfigurationProvider()` |
| `KbqDropdown.onPanelReached()`                                              | nothing: nothing subscribed to it                                                                      |
| the protected `KbqTreeSelection.getItemHeight()`                            | `options.first?.getHeight() ?? 0`                                                                      |
| the protected `KbqTreeSelection.setFocusedOption()`                         | `this.keyManager.setActiveItem(option)`                                                                |
| `KbqTagList.tagSelectionChanges`, `.shouldLabelFloat`                       | the `selectionChange` output of each tag; `!empty() \|\| focused()`                                    |
| `KbqTreeNodeOutlet.changeDetectorRef`                                       | `ChangeDetectorRef`, injected where you need it                                                        |

A subclass loses the protected members nothing read: `changeDetectorRef` of `KbqAccordion`, `KbqAccordionItem`, `KbqPasswordToggle`, `KbqIcon` and `KbqSearchExpandable`, `KbqAccordionTrigger.nativeElement`, `KbqNotificationCenterComponent.dateAdapter`, `KbqFilters.styles`, and `isHorizontalOverflown`, `isVerticalOverflown` and `child` of `KbqTitleDirective`. Inject what the subclass needs itself; `isOverflown` of the title covers both directions.

The styles lose the rules for classes nothing sets: `kbq-control_has-validate-directive` and `kbq-form-field_has-validate-directive`, left from the `KbqValidateDirective` removed in 20.0.0 (the form field, select and tree select show an error through their `ErrorStateMatcher`), and the `kbq-no-select` utility class: set `user-select: none` in your own styles.

sections.heading: Actions panel overlay container (21.0.0)
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-components(actions-panel) */}

`KbqActionsPanelConfig.overlayContainer` now names the element the panel is rendered **into**, rather than an anchor it was positioned against. The panel is pinned to the bottom center of that element and resizes with it.

What that changes for code already setting the option:

- **An element with `overflow: hidden` clips the panel**, and one that scrolls its own content scrolls the panel away with it. At `overflow: visible` the entrance animation renders the panel below the element.
- **The element is mutated while the panel is open**: it gains one child node holding the overlay, and a `static` element is promoted to `position: relative`, since the overlay is positioned against it.
- **`maxWidth` is no longer ignored** when `overlayContainer` is set.
- **A globally provided `OverlayContainer` is bypassed** while the option is set.

sections.heading: Running the migration
sections.body:
`actions-panel-overlay-container` is registered for 21.0.0, so an `ng update` to that version runs it:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:actions-panel-overlay-container --project "<your project>"
```

It only reports the call sites — there is nothing to rewrite, because the option is the same one and only its meaning changed.

sections.heading: Legacy splitter deprecation (21.0.0)
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-components(splitter) */}

`@koobiq/components/splitter` now resolves to a rewritten splitter: it lays panels out with CSS grid and adds per-panel size constraints, collapsing, snap points, full keyboard support and the WAI-ARIA `separator` pattern. The previous implementation — `KbqSplitterComponent`, `KbqSplitterAreaDirective`, `KbqGutterDirective`, `KbqGutterGhostDirective`, `KbqSplitterModule` and the `Direction` enum — moved to `@koobiq/components/splitter/deprecated` unchanged, and will be removed in 22.0.0.

**Most unmigrated imports break loudly.** `KbqSplitterComponent`, `KbqSplitterAreaDirective`, `KbqGutterDirective`, `KbqGutterGhostDirective` and `Direction` live at the `/deprecated` path only, so the build stops with `TS2305: … has no exported member`.

**`KbqSplitterModule` is the silent one — it is the case this migration exists for.** Both entry points export a class under that name, and the `kbq-splitter` selector exists on both sides, so an unmigrated import keeps compiling but now pulls in the rewritten splitter. That one projects `kbq-splitter-panel` children instead of `[kbq-splitter-area]` hosts and takes `orientation` rather than `direction`, so the group renders with no panels and no separators.

Templates need no changes of their own: once the import points at `/deprecated`, `<kbq-splitter>` with `[kbq-splitter-area]` hosts, `direction`, `useGhost`, `hideGutters` and `gutterSize` keeps working exactly as before.

sections.heading: Running the migration
sections.body:
`splitter-deprecated-path` is registered for 21.0.0, so an `ng update` to that version runs it:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:splitter-deprecated-path --project "<your project>"
```

It rewrites the `@koobiq/components/splitter` specifier to `@koobiq/components/splitter/deprecated` across every `.ts` file, and running it twice changes nothing. It does not move you onto the new splitter: that is separate manual work — areas become `kbq-splitter-panel`, `direction` becomes `orientation`, and sizes move from `min-width` and CSS `flex` onto the `size` and `minSize` inputs.

sections.heading: Overlay demotion removal (21.0.0)
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-components(dropdown, select, popover, navbar, top-bar) */}

Until 21.0.0 an open `dropdown`, `select` or `popover` panel lowered the **shared, app-wide** `.cdk-overlay-container` from `z-index: 1000` to `999` by adding a `.cdk-overlay-container_dropdown` class to it. The point was to let a panel slide under a sticky `kbq-navbar` / `kbq-top-bar` while the page scrolled. `KbqDropdownTrigger.demoteOverlay` turned that off for one trigger, and the `KBQ_DROPDOWN_HOST` marker token — provided by `KbqNavbar` and `KbqTopBar` — flipped its default to `false` so a dropdown inside the chrome would not end up behind its own trigger.

The whole mechanism was removed: the input, the token, the class and the stylesheet rule. It operated on the container rather than on individual overlays, so it could not lower a panel without lowering every other overlay — modals, sidepanels, toasts and tooltips included — and it did so from whichever component happened to open first.

**Panels now render above `kbq-navbar` and `kbq-top-bar` instead of sliding under them.** They open in the browser top layer (see Overlays in the top layer in Upgrade to Angular 21); with `usePopover: false` the overlay container stays at `z-index: 1000`, above the bars at `990`.

sections.heading: Running the migration
sections.body:
The `dropdown-demote-overlay` schematic runs automatically:

```bash
ng update @koobiq/components@21
```

Or manually:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:dropdown-demote-overlay --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: What is fixed automatically
What you need to fix manually
sections.body:
**Programmatic `demoteOverlay` access.** A read or an assignment (`this.trigger.demoteOverlay = false`) is reported with a warning rather than rewritten — deleting a statement is not always safe, and the compiler flags it anyway. There is nothing to opt out of any more, so remove the line.

**Providers the schematic could not rewrite.** A provider declared outside a provider array (`export const HOST_PROVIDER = { provide: KBQ_DROPDOWN_HOST, … };`), or an `inject(KBQ_DROPDOWN_HOST)` call, is reported as a leftover `KBQ_DROPDOWN_HOST` warning. Remove it by hand.

**`.cdk-overlay-container_dropdown` rules in your stylesheets** are dead — the class is never applied now. This is reported as a warning. If the rule was an override neutralising the demotion, it is simply redundant.

**Panels that used to slide under your sticky chrome now render on top of it.** To get that back, mark the content area below `kbq-navbar` / `kbq-top-bar` with `kbqOverlayLayer` from `@koobiq/components/core` — see [Panels under a sticky header](/en/components/core/overview#panels-under-a-sticky-header). Unlike the demotion, it moves only the panels opened from inside that area: modals, sidepanels, toasts and tooltips stay above the bars.

**`kbq-select` and popover panels inside `kbq-navbar` / `kbq-top-bar` are fixed by this release.** They applied the demotion unconditionally and had no opt-out, so they rendered behind the very chrome that contained them. No action needed — this is the bug the removal fixes.

sections.heading: App-switcher upgrade (21.0.0)
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-components(app-switcher) */}

In version 21.0.0 `KbqAppSwitcherTrigger` moved `selectedApp` and `selectedSite` from a plain `@Input()` (plus a matching `output()`) to `model()`, and a review of the component removed several members that never did anything. Template bindings keep working — `[selectedApp]`, `[(selectedSite)]` and `(selectedAppChange)` are unchanged — so only programmatic access and reads through a `#ref="kbqAppSwitcher"` template reference variable break.

| Member                                                                               | Before              | After                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `selectedApp`                                                                        | `@Input()` property | `ModelSignal` — write via `.set()` |
| `selectedSite`                                                                       | accessor input      | `ModelSignal` — **value changed** |
| `selectedAppChange` / `selectedSiteChange`                                           | `output()`          | the implicit outputs of the models above                           |
| `header` / `footer`                                                                  | properties          | removed                                                            |
| `KbqAppSwitcherComponent.isTrapFocus` / `updateTrapFocus()`                          | public API          | removed                                                            |
| `KbqAppSwitcherDropdownApp.getIcon()`                                                | public method       | removed                                                            |
| `KbqAppSwitcherComponent.activeSite` / `activeApp`                                   | protected           | removed: the context of the flyout's `kbqDropdownContent` template |
| `KbqAppSwitcherListItem.collapsed`                                                   | property            | `ModelSignal<boolean>`                                             |
| `app` / `site` inputs of `KbqAppSwitcherListItem` / `-DropdownApp` / `-DropdownSite` | optional inputs     | `input.required` signals                                           |

sections.heading: Running the migration
sections.body:
The changes are applied by the `app-switcher-signals` schematic (runs automatically):

```bash
ng update @koobiq/components@21
```

Or manually — for example, if you have already upgraded to 21.0.0. To preview without writing — `--fix=false`:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:app-switcher-signals --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: What is fixed automatically
sections.body:
**Reads and writes in TypeScript** (for receivers annotated `KbqAppSwitcherTrigger`):

- trigger.selectedApp → trigger.selectedApp(),
- trigger.selectedApp = app → trigger.selectedApp.set(app),
- trigger.selectedApp.name → trigger.selectedApp().name,
- trigger.selectedAppChange.subscribe(fn) → trigger.selectedApp.subscribe(fn) — `ModelSignal` implements `OutputRef`, so the callback signature is identical

**Reads through a template reference variable** (`#ref="kbqAppSwitcher"`, in external `.html` files and inline templates):

- switcher.selectedApp → switcher.selectedApp()

All replacements are idempotent — an access already followed by `()`, `.set`, `.update`, `.asReadonly` or `.subscribe` is left alone, so running the schematic twice does not double the call.

Note that `selectedApp()` is typed `KbqAppSwitcherApp | undefined`. Where the old property was read as non-nullable, the compiler will now ask for a `!` or a `?.` — that narrowing is yours to place.

sections.heading: What you need to fix manually
sections.body:
The schematic emits warnings for what cannot be rewritten safely:

**`selectedSite` is not rewritten, because its value changed.** The old getter returned the site with its applications already grouped for rendering; the model returns the value that was passed in. Read `trigger.selectedSite()` for the raw site and `trigger.parsedSelectedSite()` for the grouped one, and write with `trigger.selectedSite.set(site)`. `selectedSiteChange` is now the model's implicit output and emits the raw site as well.

**`selectedAppChange.emit(app)`**: no longer an emitter → `trigger.selectedApp.set(app)`.

**`header` / `footer`**: removed. The popup never rendered either, so the value was pushed into the overlay and dropped — delete the usage.

**`isTrapFocus` / `updateTrapFocus()`**: removed from `KbqAppSwitcherComponent`. Its template never bound `[cdkTrapFocus]`, so neither did anything.

**`activeSite` / `activeApp`** of a `KbqAppSwitcherComponent` subclass: removed. Each flyout of another site or group reads its site and app from the context of its `kbqDropdownContent` template, which `kbqDropdownTriggerData` fills.

**`KbqAppSwitcherDropdownApp.getIcon()`**: removed. Inline markup is sanitized by `KbqAppSwitcherIconSanitizer` and rendered by the component itself.

**Inline `icon` markup is now sanitized** against a strict SVG allow-list before it is rendered: `<script>`, `<style>`, `<foreignObject>`, HTML elements, every `on*` handler and any reference to an external resource are removed, and markup that changes shape when re-parsed is dropped entirely — in which case the row falls back to `iconSrc`. Check any icon that relies on those; prefer `iconSrc` for icons that come from a server.

The schematic does not cover the following changes — check them yourself:

**`KbqAppSwitcherModule` no longer provides `FocusTrapFactory` / `FOCUS_TRAP_INERT_STRATEGY`.** The app-switcher never rendered a focus trap, and those providers are injector-wide: they replaced the CDK inert focus-trap strategy with a no-op for every other focus trap in the same scope. If your application relied on that, provide them explicitly where they are actually needed.

**`defaultGroupBy`** now identifies a synthetic app group by its type name instead of an empty `id`.

**The popup hides itself when it scrolls out of an ancestor marked `kbq-hide-nested-popup`** (a tab body, for example). The guard that used to suppress this never passed, so the behaviour is effectively new.

The schematic matches receivers by explicit type annotation only, so aliases (`const t = this.trigger; t.selectedApp`) are left untouched — fix them by hand.

sections.heading: Button review (21.0.0)
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-components(button, button-group) */}

The review of `[kbq-button]` changed three unrelated things at once. Nothing here has a deprecation period — the old behaviour is simply gone — but only one of the changes stops your code from compiling.

**Host attributes are now chosen by host tag.** Until 21.0.0 a disabled button rendered `disabled` _and_ `aria-disabled="true"`, whatever the host element was. `disabled` is not a valid attribute on an anchor and was ignored by the browser, while `aria-disabled` on a native `<button>` merely repeated what the native attribute already said. Each host now gets the one that applies:

| Host                             | Before                              | After                                                                  |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<button kbq-button [disabled]>` | `disabled` + `aria-disabled="true"` | `disabled`                                                             |
| `<a kbq-button [disabled]>`      | `disabled` + `aria-disabled="true"` | `aria-disabled="true"` + `tabindex="-1"` + `.kbq-disabled`             |
| `<button kbq-button>`            | `tabindex="0"`                      | no `tabindex` — a native button is already in the tab order            |
| `<a kbq-button>` without `href`  | no role                             | `role="button"` — it does not navigate, so it is announced as a button |

**A button group no longer overwrites what the button owns.** `KbqButtonGroupRoot` propagated its `kbqStyle` and `color` to every nested button on each update, including buttons that set their own. It now treats such a button as the owner and leaves it alone. Its `disabled` became additive as well: disabling the group disables every child, but re-enabling it no longer enables a child that was disabled through its own input. The `disabled` getter reads `boolean | undefined` and stays `undefined` while the input is unbound, so an unbound group never force-enables anything.

**Styles.** Four physical border-radius mixins were removed in favour of logical ones, the `.kbq-progress` utility moved into `kbq-core()`, and two custom properties that nothing read were dropped.

sections.heading: Running the migration
sections.body:
The `button-state-and-styles` schematic runs automatically:

```bash
ng update @koobiq/components@21
```

Or manually:

```bash
ng g @koobiq/components:button-state-and-styles --project "<your project>"
```

sections.heading: What is fixed automatically
What you need to fix manually
sections.body:
**Buttons that own an input inside a group** are reported with a file and line number. The schematic parses your templates and reports a button only when it sits inside a group _and_ declares its own `kbqStyle`, `color` or `disabled`: ```html
``` Drop the binding if you wanted the group value, or keep it if you wanted the override. Both readings were possible before, which is why this is reported rather than rewritten. **`KbqButtonGroupRoot` and `KbqButtonCssStyler` API changes** are reported as warnings. The group's `disabled` is now `boolean | undefined`; on the styler, `nativeElement` became `readonly` and `icons` is typed `Signal` instead of `readonly any[]`, so assignments and untyped member access stop compiling. **Selectors and assertions built on the `disabled` attribute.** `a[kbq-button][disabled]` never matches now — use `.kbq-disabled` or `[aria-disabled="true"]`. Selectors targeting `

sections.heading: Button supported colors (21.0.0)
sections.body:
{/* migration-step-components(button) */}

A button's `color` accepted any `KbqComponentColors` / `ThemePalette` value, but `kbq-button-theme()` only ever styled the pairs the design system defines:

| `kbqStyle`    | Supported colors              |
| ------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `filled`      | `contrast`, `contrast-fade`   |
| `outline`     | `theme-fade`, `contrast-fade` |
